answer: Duplicates die by replay, not by name. Every submission commits a hash of its inputs and its output, and the node republishes the seen digests each epoch as a lantern anyone can check, so a copy dies on identical bytes even under a fresh label. That is what breaks a farm first: recycling one draft across fifty accounts still needs fifty distinct input sets. When the replay bites, the inviter's bond burns too, a small ember that travels back up the recruit chain, and each fake account has to buy fresh timber instead of reusing last week's.
